subject: Intermittent private-link large upload failures after cutover
messages:
From: Matt Reeves <matt.reeves@clearwaterhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:12:03 -0700
Subject: Private link: large uploads failing intermittently after cutover

Hi Naomi,

We cut over the private link to the Redwood Private deployment this morning (per the plan) and since then our nightly EHR file transfers (SFTP, ~300MB files) have been failing roughly 30-40% of the time. Small requests/queries are fine. When a transfer fails it stalls and then the client side closes the connection with a timeout. We rolled back to the previous NAT gateway as a quick test and the transfers succeeded.

Can you escalate on networking? We suspect MTU/reassembly or NAT port exhaustion but wanted your input. I've attached a short tcpdump from the client-side host and the SFTP server showing the failure window.

Attachments: tcpdump-clearwater-20270528.pcap

Thanks,
Matt

Subject: FW: Private link: large uploads failing intermittently after cutover

Team — forwarding customer's tcpdump and initial symptom set. Key notes: failures are for large files only (~>50MB) after today's cutover to our new private-edge NAT path. Customer reports rollback to their previous NAT gateway makes transfers succeed.

Attachments: tcpdump-clearwater-20270528.pcap

What I have so far:
- Source: Clearwater client host 10.12.7.34 -> destination SFTP server 172.31.24.8 over private link
- Time window: 07:45–08:30 local when failures observed
- Behavior: TCP stalls, retransmits, final connection close by client with timeout

Ask: can you triage MTU/MSS, conntrack/NAT port reuse, and any asymmetric return-paths? Also please confirm whether any security group rules could be silently dropping large fragmented packets.

I'll keep Matt updated on our progress.
—Naomi

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:05:46 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private link: large uploads failing intermittently after cutover

Investigated the capture quickly — high level notes:
- I see repeated 1460B payloads followed by bursts of 0B push/retransmits, then long gaps (200–400ms) before RTO.
- There are also duplicated ACKs pointing at possible reordering; however reordering magnitude doesn't fully explain multi-second stalls.
- No obvious TCP RST from the edge.

Immediate checks I need:
1) Kernel MSS clamp on the customer-facing edge (for tunnels/GRE/ESP we clamp to 1380 historically). If our new path is encapsulating and we didn't clamp, packets may be fragmented and dropped by intermediate hardware.
2) Conntrack/NAT port table on the edge during the window — need peak ephemeral sockets to rule out port recycling.
3) Security group stateful inspection: some middleboxes silently drop large fragmented pieces if DF isn't handled consistently.

If we can, please grab: iptables -t nat -L -n -v; conntrack -L --orig-port; and show edge interface MTU and any tunnel encap. I've attached a short config diff from the cutover candidate that may show missing clamp.

Attachment: edge-config-diff-20270528.txt

I'll stand by to push an MSS-clamp quickly if Karthik confirms.
—Vanessa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:02:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private link: large uploads failing intermittently after cutover

Checked the edge VM logs and config snapshots for 07:30–09:30. Findings:
- The edge path is using IPsec tunnel with additional 50 bytes overhead (ESP + headers). The cutover config omitted the iptables MSS clamp due to a templating issue (see diff).
- conntrack table showed high churn but not exhausted (peak usage ~74% of table). NAT translations look normal.
- Route tables look symmetric; ack path returns through the same edge. No asymmetric routing observed.

Mitigation plan (quick):
1) Apply MSS clamp on the egress chain to 1350 on the customer-facing interface to allow for encapsulation overhead: iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1350
2) Temporarily increase conntrack max to reduce recycling: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
3) If customers still see failures, enable short-term TCP keepalive/enable selective ACK (SACK is already ON) and capture after change.

I'll prepare a one-line change we can push and rollback quickly. Vanessa — can you apply the clamp and watch the next scheduled transfer?

—Karthik

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:34:01 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private link: large uploads failing intermittently after cutover

I've applied the MSS clamp to the test-edge host in the customer's region and restarted the ipsec tunnel for a clean state. Commands run (audit log attached):
- iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -p tcp --syn -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1350
- sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000

Monitoring shows a drop in retransmit events on the test flow. I've left tcpdump running on the SFTP server side and saved a second capture. I'll attach when I have a failing case, but early signs look promising.

Attachment: tcpdump-clearwater-20270528.pcap (updated)

If this holds for two scheduled transfers, propose a maintenance window to push the change to prod-edge for all private links in that region and update the cutover template to include MSS clamp by default.

—Priyom

Hi Matt — quick update and next steps: 

What we did:
- Identified missing MSS clamp on the new private-edge path that caused large packets to be fragmented after IPsec encapsulation.
- Applied a temporary MSS clamp (1350) and increased conntrack capacity on the test-edge host.
- Early telemetry shows a significant reduction in retransmits and the customer's test transfers are succeeding in the test window.

Next steps:
1) Schedule a 30-minute maintenance window to deploy the MSS clamp to the production-edge hosts for your private link (recommended window: Sat 05:00–05:30 PT).
2) We'll update the cutover config templates to include the MSS clamp and add a post-cutover verification checklist (tcpdump + quick large-file transfer).
3) We'll provide the post-change captures and an RCA doc (link to ticket below) once we complete the prod rollout.
